title: Impact
summary: Impact is the tactic covering the actions an adversary takes to degrade, disrupt, destroy, or manipulate the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of systems and data, and it is where an intrusion becomes an operational and often physical business event. Behaviours include encrypting data for extortion, deleting or overwriting data and backups to prevent recovery, inhibiting system recovery features, defacing public sites, disrupting services through denial of service or resource exhaustion, manipulating or falsifying records to undermine trust, and using destructive wiper-like techniques. Defenders receive the clearest signal of any tactic here, but usually far too late: mass file modifications and rename storms, volume shadow copy deletion, backup catalogue changes, hypervisor or virtual machine snapshot removal, service stops across many hosts at once, account and permission destruction, and storage or compute consumption spikes. Endpoint and storage telemetry, backup system logs, hypervisor events, and cloud control-plane audit records all show these actions, and alerting on the earliest of them, especially anything touching backups or recovery capability, buys the only meaningful response time available. Detection in isolation is less of a problem than acting fast enough and having a tested recovery path; the practical challenges are distinguishing destructive intent from a failed deployment or a legitimate maintenance window, preserving evidence while containing, and knowing in advance the order in which to disconnect, isolate, and restore.
objectives: Describe the range of impact behaviours, from encryption and destruction to manipulation and service disruption.
Identify the earliest observable signals of destructive activity, especially those touching backups and recovery capability.
Explain how backup architecture, offline copies, and restore testing determine whether any response can succeed.
Design alerting that separates a genuine destructive campaign from failed deployments and maintenance activity.
Sequence containment correctly to stop propagation while preserving the evidence needed for recovery and investigation.
Evaluate recovery time and data loss objectives against realistic destructive scenarios and identify the gaps.
